result.summary:
The new title screen and the attract mode are both done; all tests pass. Neither race_session.gd nor audio_manager.gd needed any change.

TITLE SCREEN: The user's image (assets/ui/title_background.webp) is drawn by a new full-window canvas shader (TitleBackdrop). It fills the window at 16:9 and at the 16:10 Steam Deck size (expand aspect) without leaving gaps. Motion is kept subtle:
- a slow Ken Burns zoom (up to 6.5 % over 45 s, focus drifting from the car towards the skyline over 72 s); it never shows an image edge,
- a slowly pulsing sun glow with a faint horizontal flare,
- thin speed streaks on the asphalt. They move with perspective towards the viewer and only appear between the road edges, never over the car, van or trucks.
All loop periods divide Godot's 3600 s shader-time rollover, so nothing jumps. The image is darkened slightly to the right and at the bottom for readability.
The logo sits top-right over the sky on a soft dark halo. The menu is on a frosted-glass card (GlassPanel: the same image, blurred via mip levels with the same zoom transform, tinted, chamfered corners, magenta-to-cyan border) over the right side of the road. Sun, skyline and the red car stay free, also at strongest zoom and at 16:10 (unit-tested). Buttons are translucent; the focus style is unchanged. MenuShell cross-fades between the photo and the synthwave background via a new field UiScreen.backdrop; all other menus keep synthwave. Checked with screenshots at 16:9 and 16:10, keyboard and gamepad hints.

ATTRACT MODE (AttractMode, a child of GameFlow; config section attract):
- After 60 s without input on the title (only while no question box is open), a 30 s demo starts in the real race scene, driven by the autopilot. It goes through GameFlow.start_attract_stage, so the title music keeps playing and nothing reaches the race flow.
- Seven scenes rotate, defined in config attract.scenes: Frankfurt approach at sunset, snow in the Pyrenees (rename of "Somport"), Paris arrival at dusk with the Eiffel tower, Köhlbrandbrücke into Hamburg at midday, night run in rain to Berlin, Venice causeway, Vienna at dawn. The next demo shows the next scene.
- Effect buses (SFX, Room, Engine, Siren, TrafficV*) are muted for the demo and restored to their previous state afterwards; a bus the player muted stays muted. The Music bus is never touched.
- Overlay: logo centred at the top (landmarks appear at the sides of the road), a DEMO badge with the scene name, a blinking "Taste drücken" bottom-left (gamepad shows only the A glyph), and a thin progress line. The HUD shows only the clock panel and speedometer (new Hud.reduced).
- Any key, gamepad button, stick push ≥ 0.5, click or touch ends the demo immediately. The event is consumed in _input before the GUI sees it; the same key, button or axis stays swallowed until released, and there is a 0.4 s guard. Result: no menu action is ever triggered.
- After 30 s the demo fades back by itself, and also when the stage reaches the finish inside the demo. The idle timer then restarts.
- Nothing is saved. In addition, leaderboard boards that only the demo seeded in memory are forgotten, so a later save writes nothing the demo touched.
- Demo timers count frame time without Engine.time_scale, so Movie Maker video seconds match. Without that, demos under load ran 21–27 s instead of 30 s.
- Debug CLI: --attract-after=<s>, --attract-scene=<index|id>, --attract-demo-s=<s>, --attract-press=<s> (injects Enter, for recordings), --no-attract, --title-time=<s>.

TESTS: tools/run_tests.sh passes: 345 unit tests including 9 new ones in test_attract_mode.gd, check_session (10), the new check_attract (13), check_escapes (2). check_attract runs the whole game headless and is now part of run_tests.sh. It covers:
- the idle timer and the 30 s duration,
- the next demo showing the next scene,
- Enter, gamepad A and a mouse click each ending the demo with no menu action, and Down working again afterwards,
- a stage finishing inside the demo,
- no file writes (MD5, size and time of savegame, leaderboards and settings, including .bak/.tmp) and no new leaderboard entries or boards in memory,
- buses muted and restored, and music continuity.
Under Xvfb with the Dummy audio driver the music player ran without a single dropout or jump back. A leak check over 15 consecutive demos showed constant object and node counts once all seven scenes had loaded once.

DOCS: docs/ui.md (new sections Titelbildschirm and Attract-Modus, files, flow, HUD, GameFlow API, debug commands incl. the Movie Maker command, config), docs/steam-deck.md, ARCHITECTURE.md §10/§13/§14.

VIDEO: Movie Maker MP4 (H.264 + AAC, 1280×720, 30 fps, 32.4 s): title with music → fade into the Frankfurt sunset demo → key press at 20 s into the demo → title. Trimmed just before the next demo's fade, with a 0.8 s fade-out.
deviations: There are 7 demo scenes, not 6: Vienna at dawn was added. The 'snowy mountain road' is a curvy Pyrenees Landstraße before the Somport tunnel (saragossa_pau km 159), named 'Schneetreiben in den Pyrenäen'. The 'autobahn rush hour' is the evening Frankfurt approach at 18:48, chosen because it echoes the title image (sunset, Frankfurt skyline); it is not a morning rush hour.

In the city scenes (Paris, Hamburg, Venice, Vienna) the autopilot follows dense city traffic at about 50 km/h, so each covers roughly 5 km in 30 s. Start points were therefore placed just before each scene's bridge or landmark. The autobahn scenes run at 140–215 km/h.

In the demo overlay the logo is centred at the top, not top-right: in the first test the top-right logo covered the Eiffel tower. The 'Taste drücken' prompt sits bottom-left, because bottom-centre covered the player's car.

Demo and idle timers count frame time without Engine.time_scale instead of wall-clock time. With wall-clock time, demos lasted only 21–27 game-seconds under load, and Movie Maker recordings would not match video time.

Added beyond the brief: --attract-press=<s> (deterministic key press for recordings), --title-time=<s> (screenshots of a given zoom phase), and clean-up of leaderboard boards that only the demo seeded in memory.

No edits to race_session.gd or audio_manager.gd were needed. The demo uses existing setup keys and, after the scene's _ready, sets vehicle.speed and hud.reduced and removes the scene's own Screenshotter (only present in --screenshot runs).
notes_for_lead: Music agent dependency: AudioManager.set_music(true) must not restart music that is already playing; the return to the title calls it through GameFlow._ensure_shell. stop_all() must also leave the music alone, because it is called at demo start and end to silence effects. If the new music source is an AudioStreamGenerator filled from the main thread, the 0.1–0.3 s hitch while the race scene builds could cause an underrun; WAV/OGG players are unaffected. check_attract finds the music player through AudioManager._music or any player on the Music bus, and treats a missing _music_wanted flag as 'requested'.

The MP4 was recorded with the current synthesized title music. After the rock theme lands, re-record with: xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x720x24" godot --path . --rendering-driver opengl3 --write-movie OUT.avi --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 1000 res://scenes/main.tscn -- --attract-after=6 --attract-press=20 (use an isolated XDG_DATA_HOME). Trim to about 32.4 s: the next demo starts fading at about 32.6 s. My ffmpeg command: -t 32.4 -vf fade=t=out:st=31.6:d=0.8 -af afade=t=out:st=31.4:d=1.0 -c:v libx264 -crf 19 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k.

Difficulty and snow agents: their traffic and grip changes will change what the demos look like (autopilot speeds, overtaking, the snow scene). Scenes are plain data in config attract.scenes (stage, from, km, hour, weather, vehicle, speed_kmh, cruise_kmh, seed). test_attract_mode validates them against the network. After merging, re-shoot the scenes, e.g. tools/screenshot.sh /tmp/a --scene=res://scenes/main.tscn --attract-after=0.5 --attract-scene=<id> --shot-times=4,12,21.

Likely merge-conflict spots, all trivial: config/game_config.json (new 'attract' section inserted between 'hud' and 'audio', next to the audio _doc line), tools/run_tests.sh (new check_attract block after check_session), docs/ui.md (Konfiguration and debug sections), ARCHITECTURE.md §10, §13 and §14.
Not done here (lead's v0.5.0 work): version number (still 0.4.0) and README.

Files to hand to the user, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/: the video movie/crossing-europe_titel_und_attract-modus.mp4; screenshots final/titel_16x9_tastatur_00.png, final/titel_16x10_gamepad_00.png, final/demo_16x9_tastatur_00.png, final/demo_16x10_gamepad_00.png; and attract_szenen_uebersicht.png (all 7 scenes plus the title).

result.summary:
The game is now clearly harder: traffic gets in the way and rain and snow are hard to handle. It stays fair, and the cautious Autopilot finishes everything without a crash. One commit on worktree-wf_e251aaee-1f3-1, no push. All 360 checks pass: 348 unit tests, 10 race-session checks and 2 network-wide police-escape checks. 142 scripts parse.

TRAFFIC (scripts/gameplay/traffic_system.gd, config traffic.*)
- Realistic speeds per vehicle type:
  - Trucks on the autobahn drive 80–90 km/h (before 110–120), buses 95–100.
  - Cars stay in the design range (110–150 on the autobahn) but respect speed limits within 0.92–1.12 × the limit, depending on the driver.
  - Fast cars appear in the left lanes, slow ones on the right.
  - No more +15 % speed bonus at night.
- Weather slows traffic. Cars go 15 % slower in rain and 35 % slower in snow (autobahn cars 72–98 km/h, trucks 54–61). Gaps are longer and lane changes slower.
- Every lane change is announced 1–1.5 s ahead with an amber indicator, drawn on cars and on trucks/buses. A screenshot confirms it renders.
- Traffic no longer clears the way. Drivers misjudge a fast car in the mirror and pull out in front of the player. They never do so closer than the player can still stop in the current weather.
- Trucks overtake trucks on roads with 3+ lanes ("Elefantenrennen"). New traffic comes in groups and platoons behind slow vehicles. Base density is 16 cars/km on the autobahn and 10 on country roads.
- The rule against rolling roadblocks was changed in two ways:
  - A car that falls back behind a slower one now keeps falling back for another 40 m.
  - Its speed margins shrink with the weather.
  - Both fix a bug the stage runs found: in snow a car hovered beside the player and blocked his overtaking lane for 52 km at 53 km/h.

WEATHER PHYSICS (scripts/gameplay/vehicle_model.gd, driving.grip_effects)
Grip is now 0.75 in rain and 0.45 in snow, and it affects every control. Values below are for snow:
- Curve limit: grip^0.75, so curves allow 0.55 of the dry grip (0.81 in rain).
- Full braking: 9.7 m/s² instead of 19.4, about half the dry value.
- Acceleration is grip-limited: 0–100 km/h takes about 8.4 s for every car.
- Steering reacts slowly (0.49 s instead of 0.12 s). After a lane change at 200 km/h the car slides 2.9 m on, so the player has to counter-steer.
- No oversteer, no spinning. Police use the same curve grip, and escaping the police is still possible everywhere.

AUTOPILOT (scripts/race/autopilot.gd)
- It adapts to the weather:
  - It plans braking with 75 % of the braking available in the current weather.
  - It brakes early behind slow traffic and treats a signalling car as already in its lane.
  - Its steering is tuned to the slower response so it does not swing.
- Bug fixed: it used to steer straight across all lanes 700 m before a fuel lane. In snow that caused a crash into a car 95 km/h slower in the middle lane. It now moves right one lane at a time, only into free gaps.

MEASUREMENTS (tests/sim/difficulty_sim.gd, before vs after; table (j) in docs/gameplay.md)
Three stages per run, 3706 km per driver type, dry/rain/snow at 07:30 and 00:30. A "naive" driver never brakes for cars. A "late" driver brakes as if the road were dry. The third driver is the real Autopilot.

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Closing speed on traffic, median, dry rush hour | 109 km/h | 112 km/h |
| Closing speed, dry night | 83 km/h | 123 km/h |
| Closing speed, snow rush hour | 78 km/h | 119 km/h |
| All lanes blocked within stopping distance, dry rush hour | 7.6 % of the time | 15.0 % |
| Same, rain rush hour | 6.6 % | 18.6 % |
| Same, snow rush hour | 2.3 % | 21.4 % |
| Lane changes needed per km, snow rush hour | 0.10 | 0.21 |
| Collisions per 100 km, naive driver | 1.86 | 3.21 |
| Collisions per 100 km, late driver (all in snow) | 0 | 0.51 |
| Collisions, Autopilot | 0 | 0 |
| Cars pulling out in front of the player per 100 km | 0 | up to 4.5 |
| Trucks side by side per 100 km | 0 s | 28 s |

The Autopilot is now 5–8 % slower in the dry, 6–16 % in rain and 9–25 % in snow.

WHOLE STAGES AND RACES (final code, Autopilot)
- 8 whole stages, 4 in snow, 3 in rain, 1 dry: 0 collisions, 0 guardrail hits, no understeer. Off-road time was at most 0.9 s, only in the fuel lane. Averages: snow 82–108 km/h, rain 100–156, dry 125.
- Kiel – Nürnberg: 27:05.5 (v0.4.0: 25:03.8), with snow on the first leg and rain on the second, no crash.
- The leaderboard starting entries (125–165 km/h average) are still within reach in dry weather. In rain and snow they are a high target. I did not change them.

VIDEO
36.7 s Movie Maker MP4, 1280×720, H.264 + AAC:
/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/difficulty/movie/schnee_autobahn_berufsverkehr.mp4
- Snow, rush hour on the A1 Hamburg – Bremen.
- The car brakes from 176 to 74 km/h behind slow traffic.
- After each lane change it slides up to 1.3 m past the lane centre and is caught by counter-steering. No collisions.

Docs updated: gameplay.md (new "Schwierigkeit (v0.5.0)" section, table (j), stage/race results, rolling-roadblock rule), renn-modul.md §10, ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§7, and the config _doc texts.
deviations: Night bonus for traffic speed removed (traffic.night.speed_factor 1.0). The Design-Dokument start value is +15 %, but faster night traffic made overtaking even easier. Night stays calmer through the daily density curve only.
Trucks and buses now drive below the car design range: autobahn trucks 80–90 km/h, buses 95–100. Cars stay in 110–150, capped by the speed limit × 0.92–1.12.

Snow slows cars by −35 % (×0.65), not the requested ≈ −40 %. This gives exactly the requested 72–98 km/h for autobahn cars; trucks drop −32 % to 54–61 km/h, inside the requested 50–70. Rain: cars ×0.85, trucks ×0.88.

The curve limit does not use the raw grip 0.45/0.75. It uses grip^0.75, giving 0.55 in snow and 0.81 in rain. Raw grip would make snowy mountain curves 73 instead of 80 km/h and autobahn curves 126 instead of 139, because the arcade curve limit is already low in the dry. Braking uses grip^0.87 (snow 9.7 of 19.4 m/s², about half) and traction 9·grip^1.25 m/s².
Shoulder grip factor changed 0.6 → 0.51. Under the new exponent this keeps the effective curve grip on the shoulder at 0.6.
Visibility in snow was not reduced further. With half braking, the curve sight check at night only has a 28 m reserve left; less sight would make curves unfair.

Two fixes beyond the original scope, both found in whole-stage runs:
- Autopilot fuel-lane approach now moves right lane by lane into free gaps; before, it steered straight across all lanes and crashed in snow.
- Rolling-roadblock rule got a 40 m hold window (traffic.side_yield_hold_m) and speed margins scaled with the weather; before, a car hovered beside the player for 52 km.
Density raised to 16 cars/km on the autobahn (was 14) and 10 on country roads (was 9).
Demo script defaults changed: tests/race/movie_snow.gd now uses hour 7.5 and is meant to run with --start-speed=120.

result.summary:
New title theme: synthwave rock / outrun, 128 bpm, E minor, 3:22.5 min, with the final chorus a whole tone up in F# minor (the racing game's "gear change"). The 8-bar intro (0:00–0:15) plays once; the 100-bar body loops after it.

Arrangement: intro, theme (hook on lead guitar), verse 1, pre-chorus, chorus 1, verse 2, pre-chorus, chorus 2 with harmony, bridge breakdown, guitar solo, final chorus, outro/turnaround back to the theme.

Synthesis: tools/audio/music_synth.py does everything offline in numpy, with ffmpeg only for the Vorbis encode.
- Drums: kick, snare and toms with 80s gated reverb, clap, 808-style hats, crash, risers, impacts.
- Bass: picked string model plus a ladder-filter synth bass.
- Rhythm guitars: power chords and palm mutes from plucked-string models, double-tracked hard L/R (the two takes correlate at about 0), through an amp model (two tanh stages at 4x oversampling plus a 4x12 cab FIR).
- Lead guitar with bends and vibrato, plus pad, arpeggio, brass, FM bells and a synth lead with harmony.
- Mix: per-track EQ, loudness-target gain staging, section automation, sidechain ducking, plate/hall/ping-pong sends, parallel drum compression.
- Master: EQ, glue compressor, mono bass, true-peak limiter.

Measured on the decoded OGG (tools/audio/music_preview.py):
- −14.1 LUFS integrated (master −14.0), loudness range 4.6 LU, true peak −1.09 dBTP, no clipping.
- Verses about 3 LU under the choruses; the bridge breakdown dips to −19 LUFS.
- 1/3-octave balance within ±3.5 dB of a rock/pop target from 63 Hz to 16 kHz.
- 101/108 bars detected as the intended chord, with every root correct.

Loop seam:
- Intro and outro end with the identical turnaround, and the compressor detector grid divides both lengths.
- Measured: the loop's playback after the seam differs from the music's true continuation by −101 dB; no step or click at the seam.
- Godot's own playback (mix_audio) jumps sample-exactly to loop_offset; a unit test checks this.

Determinism: two runs give a byte-identical OGG (render time about 5 min).

Integration: AudioManager plays audio.music_file and keeps the old synthesized loop only as a fallback (+5 dB so it keeps its old level). The API is unchanged; music_db goes from −4 to −9 dB. Loading takes 17 ms.

In-game Movie Maker check on the title screen: the music starts immediately and sits at exactly the expected level (−14.05 dB under the file).

All tests pass: 139 scripts, 338 unit tests (including 2 new ones), integration scenarios, police-escape network check. docs/ui.md has a new Titelmelodie section.
deviations: The arrangement adds a hook 'Thema' right after the intro (the loop starts there) and a 4-bar outro/turnaround besides the requested intro/verses/pre-chorus/chorus/bridge/solo/final chorus.

audio.music_db changed from -4 to -9 dB. The mastered file is -14 LUFS; the old loop was -20 LUFS. Net effect in the menu: about +1 dB on average, about +2.5 dB in loud parts compared with the old music. The synthesized fallback gets +5 dB on its player, so it keeps its old level.
Added config key audio.music_file (default res://assets/audio/music/title_theme.ogg) and an extra tool tools/audio/music_preview.py for the checks and previews.

Tonal balance and chord detection in the preview tool are heuristics: the target curve is a generic rock/pop balance, and the 7 'chord misses' are the distorted power chords' own major-third harmonic or bass passing tones.
The in-game check video shows this worktree's old title screen; the new title screen and attract mode belong to the other agent.

issues.area: Fairness: snow at night (stopping distance vs. sight)
issues.problem: In snow at night (and deep dusk/dawn, roughly 19:30–06:00) the stopping distance from top speed is longer than the distance at which the player can see traffic. Slow traffic or a queue that comes out of the fog in the player's lane can only be dodged. When every lane is taken, the collision cannot be avoided: City-Limits queues, jams at lane drops, cars behind crests. v0.4.0 had about 50 m to spare here. v0.5.0 halves snow braking (9.7 m/s²) and slows snow traffic (city cars from 26 km/h, trucks from 54 km/h), but keeps the visibility (snow 0.5 × night 0.55 = 248 m). The sight check (i5) only covers curves, not traffic. This breaks the goal stated in docs/gameplay.md:213: 'fair (alles vorher sichtbar, nichts unvermeidbar)'.
issues.evidence:
1) Analytic, with the real VehicleModel/TrafficSystem/EnvironmentModel values (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/review_difficulty/sight_table.gd). Snow at 02:00: a car is seen at a gap of about 194 m (body fog alpha 0.5), about 211 m by its tail lights. Distance needed from top speed to the slowest city car (26 km/h), with 1.0 s reaction and full snow braking: Kompakt 205 m (+5), Limousine 230 m (−20), Sportwagen 248 m (−37), GT 275 m (−65). To the slowest truck (54 km/h): Limousine −3, Sportwagen −20, GT −48 m. Even at the full 248 m, where the fog alpha is already 0: Sportwagen −14, GT −42 m. For comparison: rain at night +45…+103 m, snow by day +83…+155 m, v0.4.0 GT in snow at night about +50 m.
2) Simulation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/review_difficulty/fair_sim.gd): a human-like driver in the GT at top speed. It sees only cars that are visible through the fog (alpha ≥ 0.5) and not hidden by a crest (camera line of sight). It reacts 0.8 s after a car appears or moves into its lane, brakes with the full braking of the weather, weaves into lanes only when the gap is safe, and steers with Autopilot.steer_to. Over 618 km of snow starting 19:30 on Kassel–Würzburg, Hamburg–Hannover and Saragossa–Pau: 2 collisions and 5 cars first seen too late; v0.4.0 on the same runs: 0 and 0.
  (a) Kassel–Würzburg km 188–190.8: Würzburg city traffic at 22–25 km/h fills both lanes just past the City-Limits sign (km 190). The cars first become visible at 187–196 m with about 200 km/h closing speed; braking from 224 to 24 km/h alone needs about 197 m, even with zero reaction time.
  (b) Saragossa–Pau km 147.1: a car at 57 km/h behind a crest, first visible at 82 m with 139 km/h closing speed. Stopping needs 108 m; v0.4.0 braking needed 69 m.
No collisions and no late sightings in any other run: dry and rain at all hours, snow by day, snow at 00:30, and snow at 06:00/21:00 on 5 hilly stages (2892 km).
3) The pull-out rule itself is fair: no cut-in came too late in about 7000 km, even for a driver who ignores indicators, only notices a car once its body enters his path, and reacts after 1.0 s.
4) The Autopilot's 0 crashes do not prove fairness. _car_in_path (autopilot.gd:305) and _car_ahead_in_lane with _look_m (110–320 m, autopilot.gd:219) see every car regardless of fog or crests.
5) docs/gameplay.md:261 says the sight in snow at night is still enough 'für jede Kurve'; this was only checked for curves.

issues.problem: The tutorial stage (first stage of the first race) still gets random race weather, now with the much harsher handling: 32 % rain and 8 % snow (climate 'north'). A first-time player then gets half the braking, a slide of up to 2.9 m after each lane change and slow city traffic, without any tutorial hint or HUD warning.
issues.evidence:
game_flow.gd:264-267 calls RaceState.choose_weather(Config.data, plan.climate, …) for every stage, the tutorial included (network.json kiel_hamburg has tutorial: true; climate north = 60/32/8 % dry/rain/snow).
Autopilot, Kompakt, 07:30 (run_stage.gd):
- v0.4.0: dry 99.9 km/h (285 s), snow 100.2 km/h (284 s) – snow changed nothing.
- v0.5.0: dry 99.2 km/h (287 s), rain 91.7 km/h (311 s), snow 65.6 km/h (434 s, +51 % time), 0 collisions.
TutorialCoach.hints_for (tutorial_coach.gd:77-110) has no rain or snow topic. The implementer's report lists the missing slippery-road HUD warning as 'not done'. The stage record on the HUD (seeded, e.g. 'REKORD 3:39') is out of reach in snow.
issues.fix: Force dry weather for tutorial stages: in game_flow.gd:266, use `if plan != null and race != null and not plan.tutorial:`, or let a stage field weather: 'normal' win over region mode for tutorial stages. Add a unit test: the tutorial stage gets 'normal' for many race seeds. Also show a coach/HUD hint once at the start of the first rain or snow stage, e.g. 'Schnee: halber Bremsweg, der Wagen rutscht nach dem Spurwechsel weiter – früh gegenlenken'.

issues.area: Pull-out fairness floor at tunnel exits
issues.problem: ctx.brake_mps2 uses the grip under the player's car. Inside a tunnel that is the dry value (19.4 m/s²). A traffic car just beyond the tunnel exit in snow may therefore pull out at the dry fairness floor, which the player cannot meet once back on snow.
issues.evidence: race_session.gd:247-248: `_player_brake_mps2()` = vehicle.brake_decel_mps2(track.grip_at(pos_z, env.grip(weather))); this feeds TrafficSystem.cut_in_floor_m (traffic_system.gd:907). Example in snow with 40 m/s closing speed: the floor is 99 m with dry braking, but on snow the player needs 115 m (0.8 s reaction plus 9.7 m/s²). Not seen in the simulations; it needs a tunnel exit and a pull-out at the same moment.
issues.fix: Pass the braking for the weather grip (env.grip(weather), ignoring tunnels), or for the lowest grip over the next ~250 m, as ctx.brake_mps2.

issues.problem: The indicator is tiny at the distances where cars pull out in snow (150–230 m). It also fades with the car body's fog alpha, while tail and brake lights use light_alpha (×1.6 at night), so at night in fog it disappears before the tail lights.
issues.evidence: road_renderer.gd:915-922: the lamp is clamped to 1.6×1.2 px and the glow radius to at least 3 px. At 200 m (about 3.4 px/m) the car is about 6 px wide and the indicator a 2–4 px dot. Screenshots: clearly visible up to about 120 m, only a dot at 160–240 m; trucks and buses are fine up close (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/review_difficulty/shots/snow_day_zoom.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/review_difficulty/shots/snow_night_zoom.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v050/review_difficulty/shots/truck_night_zoom.png). road_renderer.gd:2038 and 2344 pass `alpha`, not `light_alpha` (line 1996). The fairness floor does not rely on the indicator, so this is cosmetic.
issues.fix: Draw the indicator with light_alpha at night. Give it a minimum size that does not shrink with distance (glow at least 4–5 px, lamp at least 2×2 px) so a signalling car stands out at 150–250 m.

issues.problem: Traffic still brakes at up to 8 m/s² in snow, because traffic.max_decel_mps2 and comfort_decel_mps2 are not scaled by the weather. That is close to the player's full snow braking of 9.7 m/s² and contradicts 'snow halves braking'.
issues.evidence: traffic_system.gd:930: clampf(a, -_max_decel, …); _apply_weather (lines 368-379) only scales speed, gaps and lane-change speed. Measured with the player at 150 km/h on Hamburg–Hannover and Kassel–Würzburg at 07:30: traffic decelerates harder than 5 m/s² in 0.02 % of samples in snow, maximum 8.0 m/s² (same as dry). Rare, but a player at a normal following distance can be caught by a car stopping harder than the snow allows.
issues.fix: Scale comfort_decel_mps2 and max_decel_mps2 with the weather, e.g. × grip^brake_exp (snow about 4 m/s²). The longer snow following distances (×1.8) already leave room for this.

issues.problem: _warm_up_traffic passes weather but no brake_mps2. During the warm-up (traffic_warmup, used by demo and screenshot runs and probably the attract mode) pull-out decisions use the dry floor of 19.4 m/s².
issues.evidence: race_session.gd:258-266: the ctx has no brake_mps2, and _build calls the warm-up (line 190) before the first update that does pass _player_brake_mps2(). TrafficSystem keeps the last value it got (traffic_system.gd:468), which here is the config default (dry).

issues.area: Balance: dry weather, City Limits in snow
issues.problem: For a skilled player, dry weather (55–86 % of race stages, depending on climate) is only moderately harder, while snow is much harder. In snow the City Limits turn into a long crawl. This fits the user's snow-based complaint, but should be confirmed in the next playtest.

result.summary:
I fixed every review finding on the difficulty branch except two: the design document is left for the user's OK, and the balance finding is kept as the reviewer advised. One commit (ba501ab) on worktree-wf_e251aaee-1f3-1, no push.

Tests: 352 unit tests, 10/10 race-session checks and both police-escape checks pass (0 of 2150 chases inescapable); 142 scripts parse.

Two whole races with the Autopilot (Limousine), both with 0 collisions:
- Kiel – Nürnberg with race seed 63352: 29:39.1. Snow on Kassel – Würzburg (start 23:07, at night) and on Würzburg – Nürnberg (start 12:35).
- München – Bremen with race seed 95028: 28:41.7, rain on the first leg.

1) Fairness of snow at night (medium):
- Problem: the night sight in snow (248 m) was shorter than the stopping distance with the halved braking. A slow queue at the City Limits came out of the fog too late; the Gran Turismo was up to 47 m short.
- Fix: the night visibility factor is now set per weather (`weather.night_visibility_factor`). Snow uses 0.75, on the idea that snow brightens the night, so snow at night now has 338 m of sight (19:30: 377 m).
- New traffic sight check (`sight_check.gd check_traffic`, `curve_sight.gd --traffic`, table (i6) in gameplay.md): from top speed, with 1 s reaction and the full braking of the weather, every car now stops behind the slowest traffic in every weather and time of day, counting the fog limit only. Smallest reserve on all 104 stage directions is +27.5 m.
- City Limits are now announced 4 km (333 m) ahead, with a new sign (town sign plus "in 4 km" and the speed limit) and the HUD message "City Limits Würzburg in 4 km – Tempo 50".
- The reviewer's driver simulation, snow at 19:30: before 2 collisions and 5 late sightings, now 0 and 0. No collisions at 02:00, 07:30 or 17:00, on the 5 hilly stages at 06:00/21:00 (2892 km), or in dry/rain. The one dry collision is unchanged and is the simulated driver's own lane change.

2) Tutorial stage (medium):
- Kiel – Hamburg is now always dry in races (`weather.tutorial_weather`, `RaceState.leg_weather`; same rule in `EnvironmentModel.race_weather`). A unit test checks 400 seeds per mode.
- Every rain or snow stage now shows a short HUD hint during the countdown, e.g. "Schnee: Bremsweg ×2, der Wagen rutscht nach dem Spurwechsel weiter – früh gegenlenken". The factor is computed from the config.

3) Cheap low findings:
- The pull-out fairness floor now always uses the weather's braking, including inside tunnels and during the traffic warm-up.
- Indicators have a minimum on-screen size and fade like the tail lights at night. Before/after screenshots show them clearly at 160–240 m.
- Traffic brakes more gently in rain and snow: 4 instead of 8 m/s² at most in snow. Behind the player it keeps the dry limit, so nobody rear-ends him.
- `test_design_numbers` now checks the new numbers as fixed values instead of comparing the config with itself.

Table (j) re-measured for rain and snow (dry is unchanged by these fixes). The added difficulty holds: the driver who never brakes for cars has 3.13 collisions per 100 km (v0.4.0: 1.86; before the fixes: 3.21), and the Autopilot still has 0. Docs updated in German: gameplay.md, renn-modul.md, ui.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and the config _doc texts.

What remains: some hilly stretches hide a car behind a crest until 55–90 m before it. No weather setting can fix that (it fails in the dry and in v0.4.0 too), but snow makes it more frequent; this is documented with numbers.
deviations: Traffic sight check, crests: crest line of sight is measured and reported, but it is not part of the pass criterion. No visibility or top-speed setting can make it pass. Behind some crests a car is only visible 55–90 m ahead, which fails even dry by day and in v0.4.0. The unit test and the `--no-crests` mode check the fog part, which is what the weather decides. Share of road where a car behind a crest is seen too late (Gran Turismo, per vehicle class), v0.4.0-like vs v0.5.0: dry 0.46 % vs 0.63 %, rain at night 0.63 % vs 1.35 %, snow at night 0.54 % vs 3.11 %.

City Limits are announced 4 km ahead, not 1 km. One odometer km is only 83 m of road (1.3 s at 235 km/h). 4 km (333 m) is enough to brake from top speed to city speed even in snow. 5 km would put the sign on top of the existing '25 km' destination sign, which always stands exactly 5 km before the City Limits.

Snow night visibility is 338 m (night factor 0.75 for snow) instead of 'about 330 m', which leaves +27.5 m of reserve. I chose this over two alternatives. Tail lights beyond the fog would need a much larger renderer change, because the renderer only projects the road up to the visibility distance. A snow vmax of 0.80 would by my calculation still be short, and slower top speed makes traffic easier to dodge.

The weather hint is shown at the start of every rain or snow stage (HUD during the countdown, about 7 s), not only the first one. This needs no stored state, and conditions change every stage. It is a HUD message, not a TutorialCoach hint, because the tutorial stage is now always dry.

Traffic braking is scaled by the weather except when the car directly ahead of it is the player; there the dry limit (8 m/s²) stays. Otherwise traffic could rear-end a player who brakes hard or cuts in.
The pull-out floor uses the weather grip (`env.grip(weather)`) everywhere instead of 'the lowest grip over the next 250 m'. This gives the same result, because tunnels are the only dry spots.

docs/Design-Dokument.md is not edited. It is the user's own document (@Michi) and calls its numbers starting values. The three deviations are listed in the gameplay.md decisions table, and `test_design_numbers` now checks the new numbers as fixed values.
Balance finding (dry is only moderately harder, City Limits in snow are a crawl): no change, as the reviewer recommended keeping it until the next playtest.

The 8-stage results table in gameplay.md is kept and labelled as measured before the review. After the review I measured two whole races, the driver simulations, the traffic sight check, the curve sight check (i5) for snow at night (still 0 failures, +27.8 m) and the rain/snow rows of table (j).
notes_for_lead: Please ask the user to confirm the three deviations from the design document: no night speed bonus (design: +15 %), trucks 80–90 and buses 95–100 km/h on the autobahn (design: 110–150 for all vehicles), and traffic 15 % slower in rain and 35 % in snow. If confirmed, update docs/Design-Dokument.md, section 'Verkehr' (around lines 66–75).

Cars hidden behind crests remain a residual risk. Snow makes it more frequent: 3.1 % of road points vs 0.5 % in v0.4.0. It is rare in practice: the driver simulations had 2 late sightings over about 3300 km of snow at night, both dodged, no collision. If the user finds it unfair, the options are a warning sign before blind crests on fast roads, or a lower render.hill_height_scale.

For the next playtest, ask whether dry weather is hard enough and whether the crawl through snowy City Limits (traffic at 26–39 km/h) is fun. A city speed factor of about 0.8 in snow would be a config-only change.

The attract mode (other branch) uses RaceSession. In rain or snow it will show the weather hint during its countdown, and it shows the City Limits announcement when passing the sign. If that is unwanted in the demo, add a setup flag; I did not add one.
New debug option `--race-seed=<n>` in GameFlow, used by tests/race/run_race.gd, makes race weather reproducible. Seed 63352 gives Kiel – Nürnberg snow on legs 4 (night) and 5.
Kiel – Nürnberg times are no longer comparable to the earlier 27:05.5: the first leg is now always dry, and seed and weather differ.

Merge-conflict risk with the title-screen / attract-mode / music branches: this commit touches race_session.gd (HUD messages, ctx), road_renderer.gd (indicator), game_flow.gd (weather choice, race seed) and game_config.json (weather, city_limits, traffic.weather).
Two new German HUD texts use tr()/UiFormat.t keys: 'Schnee: Bremsweg ×%s, …', 'Regen: Bremsweg ×%s, …', 'City Limits %s in %s km – Tempo %d', and on the sign 'in %d km'.
